activity_context.topic_title: Jordan Canonical Form of a 2x2 Matrix

feedback.problem:
Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ -6 & -1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every $n\times n$ matrix $A$ can be written in the form

$$
A=PJ{P}^{-1},
$$

where $J$ is a Jordan canonical form (or Jordan normal form) of $A,$ and $P$ is an invertible matrix. 

To find the matrix $J,$ we first find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}6-\lambda  & 2 \\ -6 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-(2)(-6) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +6 & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda -3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ Since we get two distinct eigenvalues, the matrix $A$ is diagonalizable, and a Jordan canonical form is

$$
J={J}_{1}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(3)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
